EXAM:  MR BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST, MR BRAIN VENOGRAM WITHOUT AND WITH  IV CONTRAST    COMPARISON:  CT head 3/29/2020, head and neck CT angiogram 1/13/2020 and carotid  Doppler 1/6/2020    FINDINGS: Again identified is small subcortical left superior temporal gyrus  hemorrhage and subarachnoid hemorrhages within the sylvian fissure and left  parietal sulci.     Susceptibility weighted imaging demonstrates diffuse cerebral venous congestion  with arterialized signal within the dural venous sinuses. These changes are  secondary to dural arteriovenous fistula between the right transverse-sigmoid  dural venous sinus junction and multiple hypertrophic external carotid artery  feeders (occipital artery, ascending pharyngeal artery and possibly middle  meningeal artery). The right ECA shows corroborative high velocity  low-resistance waveform on the carotid duplex Doppler exam. Small arterial  feeders from the internal cerebral artery has it enters the petrous carotid  canal cannot be excluded. The right transverse and sigmoid sinuses demonstrate  interval septations consistent with recanalization of previously thrombosed  sinus, likely a sequela of remote right internal jugular vein ligation performed  for a penetrating injury in the inferior neck. Also noted is severe irregular  stenosis of the left transverse dural venous sinus, presumably a sequela of high  flow from the fistula. These changes together have produced diffuse cerebral  venous congestion.     IMPRESSION:  Dural arteriovenous fistula between the right transverse-sigmoid  dural venous sinus and right external carotid artery branches, and left  transverse dural venous sinus stenosis producing cerebral venous hypertension  with small left temporal intraparenchymal hemorrhage and left temporoparietal  subarachnoid hemorrhages.    Findings were called to Dr. Kevin Barrett at 1:15 PM.

EXAM: MR BRAIN PERFUSION WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST, MR BRAIN ANGIOGRAM WITHOUT IV CONTRAST, MR  BRAIN VESSEL WALL IMAGING WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST    3D images were created on an independent workstation as ordered by the treating provider and  reviewed by the radiologist to assist in treatment planning.    COMPARISON: Outside brain MRI 08/02/2023, outside cerebral angiogram 04/20/2022, and outside brain  MRI 03/25/2022.    FINDINGS:     Brain MRI:    Allowing for differences in technique, a 22 mm lobulated extra-axial lesion in the medial aspect of  the left sylvian fissure is unchanged on studies dating back to 03/25/2022. The lesion demonstrates  a small zone of internal precontrast T1 shortening, mostly high T2 signal, and peripheral magnetic  susceptibility. There is partial, patchy internal contrast enhancement as well as thin peripheral  rim of enhancement. Please see the vessel wall imaging section below for further discussion of this  lesion.    The brain is otherwise normal. No evidence brain parenchymal signal abnormality or diffusion  restriction. No evidence of acute or chronic infarcts. No abnormal brain parenchymal contrast  enhancement.    A mucous retention cyst is noted in the right maxillary sinus.    Brain MRA:     The left middle cerebral artery appears chronically occluded at its origin. This is located  immediately adjacent to the previously described lobulated structure in the medial left sylvian  fissure. Small collateral vessels extend laterally from the right carotid terminus within the left  sylvian fissure.     The remaining intracranial vessels are normal without evidence of stenoses or occlusion. The circle  of Willis is complete with a moderate sized right posterior communicating artery and a large left  posterior communicating artery.    Brain vessel wall imaging:      Redemonstrated is the lobulated 22 mm extraaxial mass in the medial aspect of the left sylvian  fissure adjacent to the carotid terminus. This demonstrates peripheral magnetic susceptibility.  There is patchy contrast enhancement within the central portion of the lesion (10:41). This left  sylvian fissure lesion is enveloped by a large number of small collateral vessels.  It likely  represents a congenitally dysplastic and/or aneurysmal left middle cerebral artery M1 segment that  is now mostly thrombosed. Moyamoya syndrome is considered unlikely. The patchy enhancement within  the lobulated lesion may represent some component of residual lumen.  Alternatively, the enhancement  may be on the basis of vascular proliferation within or surrounding the lesion.     Despite nonvisualization of a normal left M1 segment, the left  M2 vasculature is partially  reconstituted by the large number of left sylvian fissure collateral vessels as well as left  convexity pial collaterals.     Elsewhere, no evidence of vascular mural enhancement or luminal compromise within the visualized  intracranial vessels.     DSC perfusion imaging:    Elevation of time to peak (TTP) and T-Max within the left middle cerebral artery vascular  distribution is consistent with delayed bolus arrival through collaterals in the setting of the left  M1 occlusion. Mean transit time in this same region is slightly increased. However, cerebral blood  flow is maintained at rest, including within the left MCA distribution. No clear evidence of  elevated rCBV within the brain.    Breath-hold fMRI: The fMRI study is mildly degraded by patient motion artifact; however, meaningful  results were obtained. In response to the carbon dioxide stimulus, there is asymmetric paucity of  BOLD signal within the left middle cerebral artery vascular territory with this being most prominent  posteriorly (152:18). This likely represents reduction in cerebral vascular reserve in this region  due to maximally dilated collateral vessels. Of note, cerebral vascular reserve in the right middle  cerebral artery vascular distribution appears relatively low in comparison with the right ACA and  right PCA vascular territories. However, this relatively low CVR in the right MCA distribution is  not nearly as prominent as that seen in the left MCA vascular distribution.     Otherwise, cerebrovascular reactivity is normal within the brain with expected zones of BOLD signal  dropout in the inferior temporal lobes and inferior frontal lobes bilaterally as result of skull  base magnetic susceptibility effects.    IMPRESSION:  1. A 22 mm lobular mass in the medial aspect of the left sylvian fissure has imaging findings most  suggestive of developmental dysplasia and/or aneurysmal dilatation of the M1 segment of the left  middle cerebral artery which now appears mostly thrombosed.  Given that a small amount of enhancement is noted within the lesion, some residual lumen is not  entirely excluded.  2. In association with the left sylvian fissure lesion, there is chronic M1 occlusion with  reconstitution of the left M2 branches by means left sylvian fissure and pial collaterals.   3. No evidence of intracranial vascular mural enhancement.  4. Increased TTP and T-Max in the left middle cerebral artery vascular distribution reflects delayed  flow through collateral vessels. Nevertheless, cerebral blood flow is preserved at rest.  5. Prominent reduction in cerebral vascular reserve in the left middle cerebral artery vascular  territory.
